correctness.rationale: A complete four-round EF invariant proves agreement for all ground-set sizes >=12: after three choices at most nine old labels are used, leaving three fresh labels to realize every possible fourth triple. Complete rank-one three-tuple profiles are quantifier-rank-one definable, and exact exhaustive eight-Venn-cell counting computes their pairwise directed differences for parameters 6 through 12. Direct graph verification at 6,7,8 independently matches the orbit counts. The pairwise difference certificate proves seven classes; no finite-to-infinite extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: The three-subset Kneser family is a classical natural disjointness graph family with nontrivial exceptional low orders. Exact seven depth-four classes, a sharp uniform tail cutoff of 12, and smallest stable representative of 220 graph vertices characterize the expressive-power boundary of the graph-only language. The finite certificate and structural EF invariant jointly reveal a nontrivial classification, not an arbitrary parameter slice or mere known-table recomputation.
